website.note: No discrete pipeline page; product-information pages cover the marketed Inspire device only. Investor site has no development-pipeline disclosure.

indications.indication: Obstructive sleep apnea in pediatric patients with Down syndrome (label-expansion / cognition and language outcomes)
indications.trial_name: Effects of Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation on Cognition and Language in Down Syndrome and Obstructive Sleep Apnea
indications.trial_design: Interventional, single-arm post-FDA-authorization study assessing cognitive and language outcomes in adolescents with Down syndrome and OSA implanted with the Inspire UAS system; collaboration with NIH/NIDCD.
key_milestones: Pediatric Down-syndrome indication already FDA-authorized in 2023; trial supports long-term outcomes evidence

Inspire IV.status: Approved (FDA PMA 2014; Inspire IV neurostimulator launched 2017 US, 2018 EU; CE marked 2010)
Inspire IV.indication: Moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (AHI 15-100) in adults who failed or cannot tolerate PAP; pediatric Down syndrome (FDA 2023)

Inspire V.status: FDA approved 2024 (latest-generation neurostimulator with integrated respiratory sensor; no separate sensing lead)

SleepSync platform / app / Bluetooth rem.status: FDA approved (programmer 2023, Bluetooth remote 2021); cloud patient-management platform

excluded_preclinical: Feasibility studies on next-generation neuromodulation delivery configurations (mentioned in 10-K R&D narrative, no IDE-stage clinical study disclosed)
excluded_legacy_terminated: NCT01161420 STAR trial (Stimulation Therapy for Apnea Reduction) - PHASE3 COMPLETED in 2013; supported original 2014 PMA; not an active ongoing study
excluded_other: PREDICTOR study (600-patient enrollment completed early 2024) - patient-selection / DISE-screening observational study, not a P1/P2/P3 interventional pivotal trial of a new asset
